subtitle: The Day an Empire Shot at Its Own Shadow

panels.shot: low-angle wide of Reginald Dyer silhouetted at the mouth of a narrow walled ground, soldiers behind him, a dense unseen crowd suggested by shadows within
panels.action: Reginald Dyer stands rigid at the entrance of a high-walled maidan, rifle-bearing troops arrayed behind him, as the sun of an Amritsar afternoon burns over a trapped, unseen crowd beyond.

dialogue.text: Amritsar, 13 April 1919: on a spring Baisakhi afternoon, Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer walked into Jallianwala Bagh and chose a doctrine of terror over law, shattering India’s faith in imperial reform.

i18n.hi: अमृतसर, 13 अप्रैल 1919: वसंत की बैसाखी दोपहर, ब्रिगेडियर जनरल रेजिनाल्ड डायर जलियांवाला बाग में घुसा और कानून छोड़ दहशत का रास्ता चुना, साम्राज्य सुधार पर भारत का यक़ीन तोड़ दिया।

panels.shot: montage wide, bird’s-eye over Punjab plains with smaller inset of wartime posters and a telegraph office
panels.action: Dusty Punjab plains stretch to the horizon as telegraph wires hum overhead and wartime recruitment posters peel on city walls, while a clerk in a colonial office pores over reports of unrest.

dialogue.text: The Great War had ended, but its shadow lay over Punjab. Heavy recruitment, grain requisitions and censorship had left the province tense, even as Indians waited for promised political reforms.

i18n.hi: महायुद्ध खत्म था, पर उसकी परछाईं पंजाब पर थी। जबरन भर्ती, अनाज की जब्ती और सेंसरशिप ने सूबे को तना दिया था, जबकि भारतीय वादे किए गए सुधारों का इंतज़ार कर रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium wide of an Indian newspaper stall in Amritsar, people crowding around, some holding leaflets
panels.action: In a narrow Amritsar lane, men cluster at a newspaper stall, brows furrowed as they pass a leaflet bearing the word 'Rowlatt' while a policeman watches from the corner.

dialogue.text: Instead came the Rowlatt Act of 1919, allowing detention without trial. From Delhi to Amritsar, people read the news and saw not reward for loyalty, but an empire tightening its fist.

i18n.hi: लेकिन मिला 1919 का रॉलेट एक्ट, बिना मुक़दमे की गिरफ़्तारी का कानून। दिल्ली से अमृतसर तक लोगों ने देखा, वफ़ादारी का इनाम नहीं, बस मुट्ठी कसता हुआ साम्राज्य।

panels.shot: street-level wide of an Amritsar protest meeting, with Saifuddin Kitchlew and Satyapal on a raised platform in the distance
panels.action: In an open courtyard, Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal stand on a low platform addressing a mixed crowd, hands raised, as shopkeepers in the background shutter their doors in a hartal.

dialogue.text: In Amritsar, local leaders like Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal called for peaceful protest. Hartals closed shops, meetings denounced the Act, and for a few days, defiance stayed non-violent.

i18n.hi: अमृतसर में सैफुद्दीन किचलू और डॉक्टर सत्यपाल जैसे नेता शांतिपूर्ण विरोध के लिए पुकार रहे थे। हड़तालों ने दुकानें बंद कराईं, बैठकों ने एक्ट को कोसा, और कुछ दिन की अवज्ञा अहिंसक रही।

panels.shot: tight, tense medium of a British official’s carriage moving through a crowd, with Indian police flanking
panels.action: A horse-drawn carriage carrying Kitchlew and Satyapal rolls through a guarded street, watched by startled townspeople, as Indian policemen flank it towards the Commissioner’s bungalow.

dialogue.text: On 10 April, the authorities lured Kitchlew and Satyapal to the Deputy Commissioner’s house, arrested them and secretly dispatched them from the city. The news broke like a slap across Amritsar.

i18n.hi: 10 अप्रैल को अफ़सरों ने किचलू और सत्यपाल को डिप्टी कमिश्नर के घर बुलवाकर गिरफ़्तार किया और चुपचाप शहर से भेज दिया। खबर अमृतसर पर तमाचे की तरह गिरी।

panels.shot: chaotic wide of Amritsar streets with smoke rising, a crowd surging, a European building in the background
panels.action: A crowd surges through an Amritsar street as smoke rises from the direction of government buildings, shattered glass glittering on a shopfront while a tram stands abandoned.

dialogue.text: The city convulsed. Anger spilled into attacks on banks, telegraph lines and European property; several Europeans were assaulted and killed. The protest, leaderless and furious, crossed the thin line to riot.

i18n.hi: शहर फट पड़ा। गुस्सा बैंकों, टेलीग्राफ लाइनों और यूरोपीय संपत्ति पर टूट पड़ा; कई यूरोपीय मारे गए या घायल हुए। बिना नेताओं का, उफनता हुआ विरोध दंगे की रेखा पार कर गया।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Reginald Dyer reading a telegram in his quarters at Jalandhar, lamplight harsh
panels.action: Under a harsh lamp in his Jalandhar quarters, Reginald Dyer, moustached and stiff, reads a crumpled telegram from Amritsar, his jaw tightening as a map of the district lies open on his desk.

dialogue.text: To this troubled district came Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer, commanding the Jalandhar Brigade. Telegrams spoke of murders, arson and 'rebellion'. He saw not a city in distress, but a province on the brink of revolt.

i18n.hi: इसी सुलगते ज़िले में जलंधर ब्रिगेड के कमांडर ब्रिगेडियर जनरल रेजिनाल्ड डायर आया। तारों में ‘हत्या, आगज़नी और बगावत’ की खबरें थीं। उसने एक परेशान शहर नहीं, फटने को तैयार सूबा देखा।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Dyer mounting a vehicle with troops around, early morning light
panels.action: At dawn, Dyer steps into a motor car in full field kit as Indian soldiers with rifles climb into lorries behind him, the road sign reading 'Amritsar' barely visible in the pale light.

dialogue.text: On 11 April, he moved to Amritsar to 'restore order'. His reports and later testimony show a man convinced he faced a second 1857, determined, in his words, to produce a 'moral effect' at once.

i18n.hi: 11 अप्रैल को वह ‘कायदा बहाल’ करने अमृतसर आया। उसकी रिपोर्टें और गवाही दिखाती हैं, वह खुद को दूसरी 1857 के सामने मान रहा था, और तुरंत ‘नैतिक असर’ डालने पर अड़ा था।

panels.shot: wide shot of Amritsar street with martial law notices, Dyer observing from horseback
panels.action: From horseback, Dyer surveys a main Amritsar street where notices are being nailed to walls, while Indian soldiers stand at junctions and townsfolk watch warily from doorways.

dialogue.text: As days passed, he imposed curfews, banned gatherings, and read the city’s mood through his own fear. On the morning of 13 April, he issued a proclamation forbidding public meetings without his permission.

i18n.hi: दिन बीतते गए, वह कर्फ्यू लगाता, जमावड़े रोकता, और शहर का मिज़ाज अपनी ही डर से पढ़ता। 13 अप्रैल की सुबह उसने बिना इजाज़त किसी भी सभा पर पाबंदी की घोषणा कराई।

panels.shot: sun-drenched wide of Jallianwala Bagh from above, showing the irregular walled enclosure and surrounding houses, with a gathering crowd
panels.action: Under the bright Baisakhi sun, Jallianwala Bagh lies like an irregular bowl of dusty ground ringed by high walls and houses, as streams of men, women and children trickle in through narrow gaps.

dialogue.text: That afternoon, thousands drifted into Jallianwala Bagh, a rough open ground hemmed in by walls and houses. Some came for a political meeting, others for the Baisakhi fair; many never heard any proclamation.

i18n.hi: दोपहर तक हजारों लोग जलियांवाला बाग में घुलते चले आए, दीवारों और मकानों से घिरा ऊबड़‑खाबड़ मैदान। कोई राजनीतिक सभा को, कोई बैसाखी मेले को; बहुतों ने कोई एलान सुना ही नहीं था।

panels.shot: ground-level wide inside the Bagh, people sitting, children playing, a few men speaking in the distance
panels.action: Inside the enclosure, families sit on the dusty ground, children chase each other near a shallow well, and a handful of speakers address clusters of listeners from a raised mound.

dialogue.text: Witnesses recalled a crowd unarmed and unworried. There were peasants, artisans, traders, women with infants, youths curious about politics. The air held talk, not slogans; expectation, not war.

i18n.hi: गवाहों ने भीड़ को निहत्था और निश्चिंत बताया। किसान थे, कारीगर, दुकानदार, गोद में बच्चों वाली औरतें, राजनीति को लेकर उत्सुक नौजवान। हवा में नारे नहीं, बस बातें थीं; जंग नहीं, उम्मीद थी।

panels.shot: tense medium-wide at the narrow entrance to the Bagh, Dyer and column entering single file
panels.action: At the main narrow entrance, Dyer strides in single file with a column of Gurkha and Baluchi troops behind him, their rifles held ready, the lane barely wide enough for two men abreast.

dialogue.text: Then boots sounded in the lanes. Without giving prior warning inside the Bagh or attempting to disperse the meeting peacefully, Dyer marched in with about fifty troops, roughly half armed with rifles.

i18n.hi: फिर गलियों में जूतों की धमक गूँजी। बिना बाग के अंदर चेतावनी दिए या सभा को शांतिपूर्वक हटाने की कोशिश किए, डायर करीब पचास सिपाहियों के साथ घुसा, जिनमें लगभग आधे के पास बंदूकें थीं।

panels.shot: low-angle close on Dyer’s face as he surveys the crowd, his gaze hard, hand raised
panels.action: From a slight rise near the entrance, Dyer stands expressionless, looking over the dense crowd before him, his hand raised in a curt signal as the barrels of his men’s rifles tilt towards the mass.

dialogue.text: Later, before the Hunter Committee, he admitted he had come 'to teach a moral lesson' and had decided on firing in advance. In that paused moment, he chose exemplary terror over any lesser show of force.

i18n.hi: बाद में हंटर कमेटी के सामने उसने माना कि वह ‘नैतिक सबक सिखाने’ आया था और पहले से गोली चलाने का इरादा कर चुका था। उसी ठहरे पल में उसने कम ताक़त नहीं, नज़ीर बनाने वाली दहशत चुनी।

panels.shot: wide shot from behind the firing line, rifles aimed into a packed crowd already beginning to panic
panels.action: Behind a line of kneeling and standing soldiers, rifles levelled, the image freezes on the instant they open fire towards the packed crowd, some figures already turning, others frozen upright in shock.

dialogue.text: Without ordering a warning shot or calling on the crowd to disperse, he gave the command. The rifles spoke again and again, the troops firing into the densest parts of the crowd until their ammunition nearly ran out.

i18n.hi: बिना चेतावनी की फ़ायर या भीड़ से हटने की अपील किए, उसने हुक्म दे दिया। बंदूकें बार‑बार गरजीं, सिपाही गोला‑बारूद लगभग खत्म होने तक भीड़ के सबसे घने हिस्सों पर गोली झोंकते रहे।

panels.shot: high-angle wide of the interior of the Bagh during the firing, people scrambling, some climbing walls, others near the well
panels.action: From above, people scramble in all directions within the high-walled ground, some clawing at rough walls, some pressed against narrow exits, others clustered around the edge of a low, circular well.

dialogue.text: Survivors spoke of panic in a trap: high walls, few exits, no shelter. Some tried to scale the sides, some ran for the narrow lanes, some leapt into the well. The firing lasted about ten minutes.

i18n.hi: बचे हुए लोग फँसे पिंजरे की दहशत बताते हैं: ऊँची दीवारें, कम रास्ते, कोई आड़ नहीं। कुछ दीवारें चढ़ने लगे, कुछ तंग गलियों की तरफ भागे, कुछ कुएँ में कूद गए। गोलीबारी करीब दस मिनट चली।

panels.shot: medium shot of Dyer signaling to stop, smoke hanging, soldiers lowering rifles
panels.action: Amid hanging gun smoke, Dyer raises his arm in a short, decisive gesture as the soldiers cease firing and lower their rifles, faces blank, the ground before them obscured by dust and haze.

dialogue.text: They fired some 1,650 rounds. Officially, 379 were reported killed and about 1,200 wounded; Indian leaders and local committees put the dead far higher. Dyer stopped only when, by his account, 'the crowd was dispersing'.

i18n.hi: करीब 1,650 गोलियाँ चलीं। सरकारी हिसाब से 379 मरे और लगभग 1,200 जख्मी हुए; भारतीय नेताओं और स्थानीय समितियों ने मौतों का आंकड़ा कहीं ऊपर माना। डायर ने तब रोका, जब, उसके शब्दों में, ‘भीड़ छिटक रही थी’।

panels.shot: medium-wide as Dyer turns away from the Bagh entrance, troops falling in behind him, leaving the ground
panels.action: At the entrance, Dyer turns his back on the interior of the Bagh, walking away as his troops fall into column behind him, leaving the dusty enclosure and the stunned silence within.

dialogue.text: He ordered no medical aid, imposed no curfew to help the injured, and left the wounded where they lay. He would later tell the inquiry that help arriving earlier would not, in his view, have altered matters.

i18n.hi: उसने कोई उपचार नहीं कराया, जख्मियों के लिए राहत वाला कर्फ्यू नहीं लगाया, बस जलील पड़े घायलों को छोड़कर चला गया। जांच में उसने कहा, जल्दी मदद आती भी तो ‘कुछ नहीं बदलती’।

panels.shot: somber wide of the Bagh at dusk, lanterns flickering as people search for loved ones among still forms
panels.action: At dusk, lanterns and small lamps dot the Bagh as men and women move slowly among still forms on the ground, lifting faces to the light, while the high walls loom dark around them.

dialogue.text: Night fell on a ground of moans and unanswered names. Families ventured in at risk, carrying away the injured as best they could. There were no official lists, no prompt inquest, only rumours and grief.

i18n.hi: रात कराहों और पुकारते नामों पर गिरी। जान जोखिम में डालकर परिवार अंदर पहुँचे, जितना बन पड़ा, जख्मियों को उठा ले गए। न सरकारी सूचियाँ थीं, न फौरन जांच, बस अफवाहें और मातम।

panels.shot: stark medium of Dyer before a table of British officials, Hunter Committee style inquiry room
panels.action: In a stark room, Dyer sits stiff-backed before a table of suited British officials, papers stacked, as one leans forward with a question and another scratches notes.

dialogue.text: The Hunter Committee later questioned him. Dyer calmly defended his action as necessary to prevent rebellion and stated he would have used machine guns if the lanes had allowed, insisting terror was his chosen instrument of control.

i18n.hi: हंटर कमेटी ने बाद में उससे पूछताछ की। डायर ने ठंडेपन से अपने काम को बगावत रोकने के लिए ज़रूरी बताया और कहा, अगर गलियाँ चौड़ी होतीं तो वह मशीनगनें लगाता, कि दहशत ही उसका चुना हुआ हथियार था।

panels.shot: collage shot: one side Tagore writing at his desk, the other a London drawing room with Britons toasting Dyer
panels.action: On one side, Rabindranath Tagore sits at a desk, pen poised over a letter, a medal case open beside him; on the other, a London drawing room shows well-dressed men raising glasses around a portrait of Dyer.

dialogue.text: Across India, outrage grew. Tagore returned his knighthood, calling it a badge of shame. Yet in Britain, many in the conservative press and the 'Morning Post' fund hailed Dyer as the 'Saviour of India'.

i18n.hi: पूरे भारत में आक्रोश उमड़ा। टैगोर ने अपनी नाइटहुड लौटा दी, इसे शर्म का तमगा कहा। पर ब्रिटेन में कई रूढ़िवादी अखबार और ‘मॉर्निंग पोस्ट’ फंड ने डायर को ‘भारत का रक्षक’ बताकर सराहा।

panels.shot: medium of Dyer leaving a military office, hat in hand, a clerk watching, expression unreadable
panels.action: Dyer walks down the corridor of a military office, hat in hand, passing a clerk who watches as an unseen superior’s voice calls after him, the light at the end of the corridor bright but cold.

dialogue.text: The government could not wholly ignore the outcry. The Hunter Report condemned his conduct as inexcusable and 'a grave error', and he was relieved of his command and retired, though he faced no criminal trial.

i18n.hi: सरकार पूरी तरह शोर अनसुना नहीं कर सकी। हंटर रिपोर्ट ने उसके काम को ‘अक्षम्य’ और ‘भारी भूल’ कहा, उसे कमान से हटा कर रिटायर किया गया, पर कोई आपराधिक मुकदमा नहीं चला।

panels.shot: wide shot of a Congress session, with leaders like Gandhi in the distance, a banner overhead, delegates animated
panels.action: In a crowded hall, delegates of the Indian National Congress stand and speak passionately, with Gandhi visible in the distance, as hands are raised in a vote and clerks take notes.

dialogue.text: For many Indians, Amritsar drew a hard line. Congress inquiries travelled Punjab, recording testimonies and higher casualty estimates. Gandhi, once cautious, saw trust in British fairness as broken beyond repair.

i18n.hi: कई भारतीयों के लिए अमृतसर ने रेखा खींच दी। कांग्रेस जांच दल पंजाब घूमे, गवाहियाँ और ज्यादा मौतों के आँकड़े दर्ज किए। कभी सावधान गांधी ने भी मान लिया कि अंग्रेजी न्याय पर भरोसा हमेशा के लिए टूट चुका है।

panels.shot: street-level shot of Amritsar under martial measures: Indians crawling in a lane under soldier supervision
panels.action: In a narrow Amritsar lane, men are forced to crawl on hands and knees under the watch of armed soldiers, while windows above are half-shuttered in fearful silence.

dialogue.text: In the days after, further punitive measures deepened humiliation. In one Amritsar lane, people were compelled to crawl as punishment for an assault on a missionary. Such scenes fixed the sense of a rule propped by fear.

i18n.hi: बाद के दिनों में सज़ाई कदमों ने अपमान और गहरा कर दिया। अमृतसर की एक गली में मिशनरी पर हमले की सज़ा के रूप में लोगों को रेंगकर चलने को मजबूर किया गया। ऐसे मंज़र ने डर पर टिके राज की तस्वीर पक्की कर दी।

panels.shot: present-day wide of the Jallianwala Bagh memorial, flame and names on a wall, visitors walking silently
panels.action: In the present, visitors move quietly past the stone memorial and eternal flame at Jallianwala Bagh, pausing before a wall etched with names as the old narrow lanes still enclose the ground.

dialogue.text: Today, Jallianwala Bagh stands as a memorial, its walls and narrowed exits still bearing witness. Reginald Dyer’s ten minutes of fire revealed how an empire, ruled by fear, could destroy the very consent it claimed.

i18n.hi: आज जलियांवाला बाग एक स्मारक है, जिसकी दीवारें और तंग निकास आज भी गवाही देते हैं। रेजिनाल्ड डायर की उन दस मिनट की गोलियों ने दिखा दिया कि डर पर टिका साम्राज्य कैसे अपनी ही सहमति तोड़ डालता है।

subtitle_i18n.en: The Day an Empire Shot at Its Own Shadow
subtitle_i18n.hi: वो दिन, जब साम्राज्य ने अपनी ही परछाईं पर गोली दागी
